title: Japan's New Vending Machines Make Fresh Matcha
paragraphs: How strong do you like your matcha? Well, in Japan, you'll soon be able to choose from five different strengths — all with the press of a button.
New vending machines are coming to Japan that make fresh matcha.

The machines are a little different from normal drink vending machines. Instead of selling drinks in bottles or cans, they prepare each cup of matcha after the customer presses a button. The idea is to give customers a drink that tastes like matcha made by hand.
The machines were made by two Japanese companies working together, Toyo Vending and Ito En.
Toyo Vending already makes vending machines that grind coffee beans and prepare each cup fresh. Now, it's looking to bring similar technology to matcha.
Drinks company Ito En will supply the matcha powder, which is made from carefully chosen tea leaves.
Customers will be able to choose from five different strengths of matcha, as well as different drinks, including matcha lattes.
Matcha has become increasingly popular around the world. In 2025, Japan exported 43% more green tea than the year before, partly because of growing demand for matcha.
And with more international tourists visiting Japan, Toyo and Ito En believe their machines will make it easier for visitors to try freshly prepared matcha.

The companies plan to put the machines in busy places, including train stations, airports, shopping areas, highway rest stops and areas that are popular with tourists. The first machines are expected to appear this month, although no specific locations have been shared yet.
So for people who enjoy freshly made matcha, there'll soon be a new way to get a cup without going to a cafe!
